sources: Grafana BOOHTACORD Runtime dashboard at fixed window
Grafana BOOHTACORD Traces dashboard at fixed window
Grafana Explore: Prometheus instant queries ending at the window boundary
Grafana Explore: Tempo TraceQL status=error search
trace_findings: The all-services error search displayed 19 traces: 11 Android api.request, 1 Android realtime.reconnect, 4 macOS api.request, 2 Windows api.request and 1 Windows realtime.reconnect.
The identified-session dashboard additionally showed a Windows voice.join and a Web api.request error outside that search result. Search results are therefore not a complete error census.

An Android api.request trace ran for 3m21s with a client error and no server span. Several neighboring Android api.request errors lasted about 19-25s. This supports a client-to-server delivery failure but does not identify the network cause.

A Web client api.request for DELETE /api/v1/voice/leases/{leaseID} had span status error while the corresponding API span and HTTP response were 204. The deployed client classification is inconsistent with the successful response; exact cause remains unproven.
The selected media sample showed screen sender FPS below the target with no measured packet loss. Static or low-motion content could explain low encoded FPS, so this is not a confirmed quality fault.
change: Runtime dashboard traffic, error share and p95 use the selected time range instead of cumulative counters; p95 excludes WebSocket and NaN routes without samples.
validation: Grafana Explore accepted the equivalent 3h histogram_quantile rate query and returned 18 finite HTTP routes after excluding WebSocket and NaN
Production Runtime dashboard import confirmed: 3309 interval requests and 0% 5xx in the fixed window
limitations: Full per-trace enumeration was not possible through the available Grafana UI. Tempo and Prometheus private APIs were not reachable from this workstation and SSH authentication to the monitoring host failed.
Full per-trace enumeration and client transport root cause remain unverified.
Client errors lack enough safe error classification attributes to distinguish timeout, cancellation, DNS and transport failure.
No private account, session, trace, token or media identifiers are stored in this record.
